name: Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn al-Sarī ibn Sahl al-Zajjāj
summary: The glass-cutter of Baghdad who left Thaʿlab's circle for al-Mubarrad's; author of Maʿānī al-Qurʾān wa-iʿrābuh and teacher of al-Zajjājī and Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī.
bio: Al-Zajjāj earned his living cutting glass, as his name says. He began with the Kufan Thaʿlab and went over to al-Mubarrad, as al-Zubaydī tells in the story of al-Mubarrad's first circle in Baghdad: sent to break it up, he found the newcomer the better reasoner and stayed with him, working at his trade a few days a month to live and paying his teacher an allowance. Al-Zubaydī places him first in the ninth Basran generation, 'the companions of al-Mubarrad'.

He later taught the son of the vizier ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Sulaymān and became a boon companion of the caliph al-Muktafī. His Maʿānī al-Qurʾān wa-iʿrābuh explains the Qurʾān verse by verse as grammar, and his short book on the nouns that take or refuse tanwīn (Mā yanṣarif wa-mā lā yanṣarif) is still printed. Al-Zajjājī took his name from him, and Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī was his student. He died in Baghdad in 311/923.
